# Implementation Plan: crews pidAlive false-positive (recycled-PID hardening)

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-10. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

> **Phase-4 multi-model review converged this plan** (Claude + Codex + Copilot). The
> original "fail-closed → `pidAlive:false`" design was refined to a **tri-state**
> determination after Copilot caught that fail-closing an *unverifiable* (transient
> CIM-null) PID to `false`/`dead` would route **false `member-crashed` notifications**
> (v3.13 crash sweep at `member-crash-notifications.js:292`), and Codex caught a
> broken integration test plus a non-Windows over-claim. See the collapsed
> `<details>` review block at the bottom.

## Overview

`crews` `list-members` / `getMemberHealth` (`hooks/health.js`) reports
`pidAlive: true` for members whose Windows Terminal tabs died days ago. The
operator observed 11 `pidAlive:true` members on the `ralph-pipeline` crew when
only 4 were genuinely active; the other 7 had last turns 3000–21000 minutes old
with dead tabs. Root cause: `getMemberHealth` computes
`pidAlive = isProcessAlive(launcher.pid)` — a **bare** check that only asks "is
*some* process alive at this PID?" Windows recycles the dead launcher's PID onto
an unrelated live process, and the never-pruned `launcher.pid` keeps pointing at
it, so the stale PID reads alive indefinitely. A second leak is the v1.2.12
deferred "Hole #3": `isProcessAlive` returns `true` on `EPERM`, so a foreign PID
also reads alive.

The fix makes `pidAlive` a **verified tri-state** by reusing the existing v3.6.6
recycle-safety primitive (`verifyLauncherRecycleSafety` + `describeProcess` in
`hooks/actors.js`, already used fail-closed by `/stop-member`):

- `true` — CIM verified the PID is **this member's** launcher pwsh (image is
  pwsh/powershell AND the command line carries the recorded launcher-script
  basename / `spawn-launchers`+member marker).
- `false` — **definitively not** this member's launcher: ESRCH (PID gone) OR CIM
  returned a process whose image/command line proves it is a recycled/foreign
  process.
- `null` — **unverifiable**: CIM could not resolve the PID (transient failure /
  inaccessible), or we are on a non-Windows platform where CIM-based verification
  is unavailable.

`deriveHealthState` already maps these three states correctly (it predates this
change): `false → dead`; `null → dead` if the heartbeat is stale else `unknown`;
`true → alive`/`quiet` by heartbeat freshness. The operator requirement — never
report a dead member as `alive` — is met because `alive` now requires a *verified*
launcher. Critically, an *unverifiable* PID becomes `null` (NOT `false`), so a
transient CIM failure on a genuinely-alive member with a fresh heartbeat reads
`unknown` (honest) rather than a false `dead`, and the v3.13 crash sweep (which
only fires on `state === 'dead'`) does not emit a false `member-crashed`.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

uninitialized by design.)*

- `hooks/health.js:66` `getMemberHealth`; `:72` the bare
  `pidAlive = launcher ? isProcessAlive(launcher.pid) : null`.
- `hooks/health.js:13` `isProcessAlive` — `EPERM → true` is Hole #3.
- `hooks/health.js:25` `readLauncherPid` parses only `{ pid, startedAt }` — does
  NOT read `scriptPath` (needed for the preferred recycle match).
- `hooks/health.js:46` `deriveHealthState` — `:53` `false→dead`; `:54-58`
  `null→dead`(stale)/`unknown`(recent); `:60-63` `true`→`alive`/`quiet`.
  **Unchanged by this plan** — it already handles the tri-state.
- `hooks/actors.js:2208` `verifyLauncherRecycleSafety(info,{memberName,launcherScriptPath})`
  → `{ ok, reason }`, fail-closed (exported at `:3146`).
- `hooks/actors.js:1977` `describeProcess(pid)` → `{ name, parentProcessId,
  commandLine }` | `null` via CIM `Win32_Process`. **NOT exported** today.
- `hooks/actors.js:2295-2313` — the stop-time guard is the exact call pattern to
  mirror, including the injectable `getLauncherInfo` seam its tests use.
- `launcher.pid` (written at `spawnMember`, `hooks/actors.js:~2620`) carries
  `{ pid, startedAt, scriptPath }`; legacy files lack `scriptPath`.
- Consumers: `hooks/crews.js:149` (`snapshotCrew`/`list-members`, per-member,
  ~298 members) and `hooks/member-crash-notifications.js:292` (crash sweep —
  `if (!health || health.state !== 'dead') continue;`). The crash sweep is the
  reason unverifiable must map to `null`, not `false`.

### Technical Constraints
- **Require cycle is load-safe:** `health.js` top-level-requires `actors.js`;
  `actors.js` requires `health.js` only lazily (inside functions at
  `:1093,:1167`). Adding `describeProcess` + `verifyLauncherRecycleSafety` to
  health.js's existing top-level `require('./actors')` destructure is safe.
- **Return-shape contract is pinned:** v3.13.0 added `sessionId/createdBy/role/...`
  and the manifest field count is pinned at 51. `pidAlive` is **already** a
  `true|false|null` tri-state field, so the tri-state determination needs NO
  shape change — only the *value* logic changes.
- **Performance:** `getMemberHealth` runs per-member in `list-members`. The cheap
  `isProcessAlive` ESRCH pre-check returns `false` for the dead-PID majority
  WITHOUT a CIM spawn, bounding CIM calls to live-PID launcher records (~11 of
  298 in the live evidence).
- **Windows-only primitive:** `verifyLauncherRecycleSafety`/`describeProcess` are
  CIM-based. On non-Windows we cannot verify launcher ownership, so the
  never-false-positive **guarantee is explicitly Windows-scoped**; non-Windows
  maps unverifiable-but-live PIDs to `null` (never a verified `alive`).

## Approach

### Architecture
A `resolvePidAlive(launcher, name, opts)` helper in `hooks/health.js` owns the
verified tri-state determination; its result feeds the **unchanged**
`deriveHealthState`. Verification reuses the audited v3.6.6 primitive so the
health surface and `/stop-member` share one definition of "is this PID this
member's launcher."

```
resolvePidAlive(launcher, name, { describeProcess, isProcessAlive, platform }):
  if !launcher:                 return null              # missing launcher.pid (unchanged fallback)
  cheap = isProcessAlive(launcher.pid)
  if cheap === false:           return false             # ESRCH — definitively gone, NO CIM (perf guard)
  if platform === 'win32':
     info = describeProcess(launcher.pid)
     if !info:                  return null              # CIM-null: UNVERIFIABLE (transient) -> unknown, NOT false
     safety = verifyLauncherRecycleSafety(info,
                { memberName: name, launcherScriptPath: launcher.scriptPath })
     return safety.ok ? true    # verified this member's launcher
                      : false   # CIM resolved a foreign/recycled process -> definitively dead
  else:                                                   # non-win32: CIM unavailable (documented gap)
     return null                                          # cannot verify ownership -> never claim verified-alive
```

Key reconciliation (the Phase-4 convergence point):
- **Definitive disconfirmation → `false`**: ESRCH, or CIM resolves a process that
  is verifiably NOT this launcher (foreign image, or pwsh with a non-matching
  command line). These are genuinely dead → `state: dead` → crash sweep MAY fire
  (correct).
- **Unverifiable → `null`**: CIM-null (transient/ inaccessible) or non-Windows.
  `deriveHealthState` then uses the heartbeat: fresh → `unknown` (honest), stale →
  `dead`. The crash sweep skips `unknown`, so no false `member-crashed`.
- **Verified → `true`**: only a CIM-confirmed pwsh launcher with a matching
  command line. This preserves genuine `alive` members.

Seams (`describeProcess`, `isProcessAlive`, `platform`) are injectable via an
optional 4th `opts` arg on `getMemberHealth` (defaults = real impls), so unit
tests never spawn real processes.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Verified tri-state `pidAlive` determination in `getMemberHealth` reusing
  `verifyLauncherRecycleSafety` + `describeProcess` (Windows).
- **Unverifiable (CIM-null / non-Windows) → `null`** so the v3.13 crash sweep does
  not over-fire `member-crashed` and the health surface stays honest.
- Closing Hole #3 (EPERM no longer bare-`true`; it routes through CIM verification).
- Exporting `describeProcess` from `actors.js`; reading `scriptPath` from
  `launcher.pid` in health.js.
- Unit + integration test updates via injected seams / a verified pwsh launcher
  fixture (no spurious real-process dependence on `node.exe` being an "alive
  launcher").
- Version bump + marketplace sync + CHANGELOG + plugin AGENTS.md note.

### Out of Scope
- Changing `deriveHealthState` (it already handles the tri-state correctly).
- Changing the `getMemberHealth` return-object **shape** / 51-field manifest pin.
- Pruning stale `launcher.pid` files (read-only health surface; risks racing live
  launchers).
- A non-Windows CIM-equivalent recycle check (documented platform gap; non-Windows
  maps unverifiable-live → `null`).
- The heartbeat-fresh CIM short-circuit optimization (optional; Open Questions).
- The sibling `crews-codex-member-tab-title-not-renamed` actors.js changes — a
  separate task; this plan only adds one export line to actors.js.

## Risk Areas
- **Performance on a 298-member crew.** Mitigated by the ESRCH cheap pre-check
  (CIM only fires for live-PID launcher records). Residual: many dead PIDs recycled
  onto live processes → more CIM spawns; optional heartbeat-fresh short-circuit
  noted in Open Questions.
- **actors.js shared with sibling task.** This task only adds one `module.exports`
  line; the sibling rewrites launcher builders. **Impl must rebase onto whichever
  of the two ships first** (lead-serialized — codexu AGENTS.md same-plugin rule).
- **Existing-test regressions (the Phase-4 catches).** The new default path calls
  real `describeProcess`, so (a) `health.test.js` alive/quiet/shape fixtures using
  PID 111 and (b) `integration/list-members-health.test.js`'s real-`node.exe`
  `alivemember` will mis-classify unless updated. Both are in scope with explicit
  ACs. The two flipped `health.test.js` assertions (`EPERM→alive`, "pid reuse is
  not resisted") encode the OLD buggy contract; the flip is the point — call it out
  in the PR body.
- **One-time crash-sweep burst for already-dead members.** Members whose recycled
  PID had been falsely reading `alive`/`quiet` (so the sweep skipped them) will, on
  the first post-fix sweep, correctly classify `dead` (verified-foreign → `false`)
  and may emit one `member-crashed` each. This is the sweep finally doing its job;
  the v3.13 generation-scoped latch bounds it to one per member, and guards #2
  (intentional-shutdown) / #5 (ownership) further limit it. Documented as an
  accepted, correct secondary effect — NOT a regression.
- **Transient CIM failure on a live member.** Maps to `null` → `unknown` (fresh
  heartbeat) — no false `dead`, no false crash. Self-heals next `list-members`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 (recycled-PID, the headline bug): `platform:'win32'`, injected
  `isProcessAlive→true`, injected `describeProcess` returning EITHER
  `{ name:'chrome.exe', commandLine:'...' }` (foreign image) OR
  `{ name:'pwsh.exe', commandLine:'pwsh -File C:/other/thing.ps1' }` (pwsh but the
  command line lacks this member's launcher-script basename / `spawn-launchers`+member
  marker) → `pidAlive === false` and `.state === 'dead'`.
- [ ] AC2 (genuinely-alive preserved): `platform:'win32'`, injected
  `isProcessAlive→true`, injected `describeProcess → { name:'pwsh.exe',
  commandLine:'pwsh -File <spawn-launchers>/<name>-<ts>.ps1' }` (matching the
  `launcher.pid.scriptPath` basename) + recent heartbeat → `pidAlive === true`,
  `.state === 'alive'`.
- [ ] AC3 (unverifiable CIM-null → `null`, NOT `false`): `platform:'win32'`,
  injected `isProcessAlive→true` (does not short-circuit), injected
  `describeProcess → null` → `pidAlive === null`; with a RECENT heartbeat
  `.state === 'unknown'` (NOT `dead`), and with a STALE heartbeat `.state === 'dead'`
  (via the existing `deriveHealthState` null branch). This is the EPERM/Hole-#3
  closure: EPERM no longer yields a bare `true`.
- [ ] AC4 (no false `member-crashed` on transient unverifiable): a member with a
  fresh heartbeat whose `describeProcess` returns `null` classifies `state ==='unknown'`,
  and `sweepMemberCrashNotifications` emits ZERO `member-crashed` envelopes for it
  (guard at `member-crash-notifications.js:292` skips non-`dead`).
- [ ] AC5 (verified-foreign → `dead` IS sweep-eligible): a member whose
  `describeProcess` returns a foreign live process → `pidAlive:false`,
  `state:'dead'`; the crash sweep treats it as high-confidence dead (subject to the
  existing latch/guards). Pins that definitive disconfirmation still routes a crash.
- [ ] AC6 (ESRCH short-circuit / performance): cheap `isProcessAlive === false` →
  `pidAlive === false` WITHOUT invoking `describeProcess` — a `describeProcess`
  spy/seam records ZERO calls for that case.
- [ ] AC7 (missing launcher.pid fallback unchanged): no `launcher.pid` →
  `pidAlive === null`; existing stale→`dead`/recent→`unknown` fallback preserved.
- [ ] AC8 (legacy launcher.pid without scriptPath): verification falls back to the
  `spawn-launchers` dir + member-name match and still classifies a genuine legacy
  launcher as `pidAlive:true`.
- [ ] AC9 (non-Windows, guarantee Windows-scoped): `platform` non-`win32`,
  injected `isProcessAlive→true` → `pidAlive === null` (cannot verify ownership;
  never a verified `alive`); `isProcessAlive→false` (ESRCH) → `pidAlive === false`.
  A test pins this and the `health.js` comment documents the platform gap.
- [ ] AC10 (return-shape unchanged): the `getMemberHealth` return object keeps every
  pre-existing key (the `health.test.js` `PREV_FIELDS` + `NEW_FIELDS` lists still all
  present); only `pidAlive` *values* change. The 51-field pin and
  `tests/protocol-manifest.test.js` are untouched.
- [ ] AC11 (existing fixtures migrated): the existing `health.test.js`
  alive/quiet/shape fixtures (the PID-111 cases at ~lines 70-83, 133-175) are updated
  to inject a matching `describeProcess` seam so they keep classifying `alive`/`quiet`;
  the two stale assertions (~line 51 `EPERM→alive`; ~lines 94-97 "pid reuse is not
  resisted") are flipped to the new verified expectations.
- [ ] AC12 (integration test fixed): `tests/integration/list-members-health.test.js`
  no longer asserts that a raw `node.exe` PID is an `alive` launcher; its
  `alivemember` fixture is a genuine verified `pwsh -File <spawn-launchers/...>`
  launcher (with a matching `launcher.pid.scriptPath`) OR is otherwise made
  consistent with verified semantics, and the suite passes.
- [ ] AC13 (crash-test audit): `tests/member-crash-notifications.test.js` is audited;
  any PID-stubbed-alive launcher fixture that now mis-classifies under verification is
  updated, and the suite passes.
- [ ] AC14 (suite green + typecheck): `cd ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews &&
  node tests/run.js` passes (Git Bash first on PATH); `node --check hooks/health.js`
  and `node --check hooks/actors.js` pass.
- [ ] AC15 (tests don't spawn real CIM): all NEW unit cases use injected
  `describeProcess`/`isProcessAlive` seams; no real CIM/tasklist spawn in the unit
  test path. (The integration test may spawn a real pwsh by design.)
- [ ] AC16 (`describeProcess` exported): `require('../hooks/actors').describeProcess`
  is a function; `verifyLauncherRecycleSafety` remains exported.
- [ ] AC17 (release surface): `node scripts/bump-version.js <x.y.z>` updates the 6
  version-bearing files (3 plugin manifests + 3 marketplace indexes) + asserts
  `tests/version.test.js`; `node tests/version.test.js` passes; CHANGELOG has a

## Suggested Decomposition

All three stories touch the **same plugin** (`crews`). Per the codexu AGENTS.md
parallel-spawn rule, two impls against the same plugin produce conflicting
version-file / `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md` writes, so they MUST be serialized
into one impl member. US-002 depends on US-001's code; US-003 (version/docs)
depends on a green US-001+US-002. One serial cluster, one impl member.

### Cluster: pidalive-verified-health
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=`hooks/health.js`, `hooks/actors.js`,
  `tests/health.test.js`, `tests/integration/list-members-health.test.js`,
  `tests/member-crash-notifications.test.js`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the 3
  plugin manifests + 3 marketplace indexes + `tests/version.test.js`;
  exclusive=none; risk=high (same-plugin version/docs writes).
- `execution_mode` rationale: Single plugin, single file-set, ordered dependencies
  (tests need the code; the version bump needs green tests). Splitting into parallel
  members would conflict on the shared version stamps and the AGENTS.md/CHANGELOG
  prepends. Execute serially as one impl member.

Parallel handoff (single serial cluster — the serial handoff in **Next Step** is
the recommended path): `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-pidalive-false-positive-recycled-pid/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-pidalive-false-positive-recycled-pid/suggested-decomposition.json`

Three reviewers ran in parallel in autonomous mode. The headline outcome: the
plan moved from a binary **fail-closed (`pidAlive:false`)** design to a
**tri-state (`true`/`false`/`null`)** design, because Copilot caught that
fail-closing an *unverifiable* PID to `dead` would emit **false `member-crashed`
notifications** (v3.13 crash sweep, `member-crash-notifications.js:292`), and
Codex caught a broken integration test (`tests/integration/list-members-health.test.js`)
plus a non-Windows over-claim.

| ID | Sev | Source | Finding (resolved) |
|----|-----|--------|--------------------|
| F-009 | High | copilot | Unverifiable→`false`→`dead` would route false `member-crashed`. → Tri-state: CIM-null→`null` (unknown), only definitive disconfirmation→`false`. |
| F-003 | High | codex | Non-Windows bare `true` could report a recycled PID alive. → Non-Windows unverifiable-live→`null`; guarantee Windows-scoped. |
| F-004 | High | codex | `tests/integration/list-members-health.test.js` asserts a raw `node.exe` PID is an `alive` launcher; verifier breaks it. → In scope; verified pwsh fixture (AC12). |
| F-010 | High | copilot | `tests/member-crash-notifications.test.js` PID-stubbed-alive fixtures break. → Audit + update (AC13). |

| F-008 | Med | codex | Whole-suite AC omitted the breaking integration test. → AC12/AC13 added. |
| F-011 | Med | copilot | AC3 conflated "verified-not-this" vs "temporarily unverifiable". → Split AC3 (null) / AC5 (foreign→dead). |
| F-001 | Med | claude | Non-Windows behavior change had no AC. → AC9. |
| F-002 | Low | claude | AC1-AC3 under-specified seam inputs. → Concrete inputs added. |
| F-006 | Low | codex | "7 stamps" vs "6 + version test" inconsistent. → Standardized. |
| F-007 | Low | codex | Parallel handoff unnecessary for a single serial cluster. → Serial is recommended path. |
